description:
Belver Castle stands on a bend of the Tagus river in what is now the Portalegre district, a Hospitaller stronghold whose origins trace back to a specific royal act: in 1194, King Sancho I granted the Hospitallers this land on the explicit condition that they build and hold a castle here, part of a broader effort to fortify the Tagus as a defensive line during the Reconquista period. The order acted quickly — construction followed from about 1210 to 1212, a remarkably short span for a medieval fortress of this scale.

The castle's role shifted with the crown's needs over the following decades. Under King Sancho II, who reigned from 1223 to 1248, Belver served as a royal treasury, a function that speaks to both its defensibility and its strategic position along the river. By the 1330s, the castle had become an important Hospitaller commandery, administering surrounding lands and resources on the order's behalf — one node in a wider network rather than an isolated outpost.

Belver's military value was tested again in the late 14th century: after the 1383–85 crisis that saw Portugal's independence contested against Castile, the castle was reinforced under Nuno Álvares Pereira, the military commander whose campaigns were pivotal to securing the kingdom's succession. The structure survived largely intact until 1755, when the great Lisbon earthquake — felt across much of Portugal — caused damage to the castle, as it did to countless buildings nationwide. Belver's historical significance was formally recognised in 1910, when it was designated a National Monument.

The Hospitallers who built Belver are sometimes attached to a specific founder's name in popular sources, but these accounts conflict with one another, so it's more accurate to credit the order as a whole — the Hospitallers, acting under Sancho I's 1194 grant — rather than name an individual builder.

The GetYourGuide product covering Belver is a guided tour departing from Lisbon, not a standalone entry ticket — Belver is roughly a two-hour drive from the capital, and transport is built into the tour. Visitors should confirm exact pickup times, duration and what's included directly at booking, since this runs as a full-day excursion rather than a short, self-guided castle visit.
